# Original Assignment

> **Which is the best team ever in Italian soccer?**
>
> This challenge explores all matches of Italian soccer Serie A league from 1993 to current year. The dataset is contained in the website [football-data.co.uk](http://www.football-data.co.uk/italym.php).
>
> ### Challenges
>
> 1. Think about how to scrape the data from the website, but write no code at this stage.
> 2. Ask AI to write code to import data by scraping the website. Select only columns Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG (home team goals), FTAG (away team goals) and filter rows with a valid (not NA) Date.
> 3. Using dplyr and tidyr packages (no for loops!), compute statistics for every team (matches, wins, loses, draws, points, points per match). Hint: mutate a column with the outcome of the match (for instance, H = home teams wins, A = away team wins, P = draw). Then group by team and outcome (home and away) and hence spread the outcome. Do this step without the use of AI.
> 4. Come up with at least 3 data questions on the data at hand. Just write the questions, do not find the answers.

# Challenge 1: Web Scraping Strategy

Football-Data provides Serie A match results as season-specific CSV files. The proposed approach is to read the Italian league webpage, collect the links ending in `I1.csv`, identify the starting year of each season, and select seasons from 1993/94 onward. Then, we import and combine the files, retain the five required variables, and remove observations with missing dates. This avoids downloading every season manually.

# Challenge 2: Importing and Cleaning the Data

## Setup

Install the packages **once in the RStudio Console** if needed:

`install.packages(c("tidyverse", "rvest", "rmarkdown", "knitr"))`

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
```

## Find the Serie A CSV files

Read the actual page URL (do not put Markdown link syntax inside `read_html()`). Extract relative or absolute CSV links and normalize them with `url_absolute()`.

```{r scrape-links}
source_url <- "https://www.football-data.co.uk/italym.php"

page <- read_html(source_url)

serie_a_urls <- page |>
  html_elements("a[href]") |>
  html_attr("href") |>
  na.omit() |>
  url_absolute(source_url) |>
  str_subset(regex("/mmz4281/[0-9]{4}/I1\\.csv(?:[?#].*)?$", ignore_case = TRUE)) |>
  unique()

seasons <- tibble(url = serie_a_urls) |>
  mutate(
    season_code = str_match(url, "/mmz4281/([0-9]{4})/I1\\.csv")[, 2],
    year_code = as.integer(str_sub(season_code, 1, 2)),
    start_year = if_else(year_code >= 93,
                         1900L + year_code,
                         2000L + year_code)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(start_year),
         start_year >= 1993,
         start_year <= as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"))) |>
  distinct(season_code, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(start_year)

if (nrow(seasons) == 0) {
  stop("Nessun URL Serie A trovato: controllare la pagina Football-Data.")
}

seasons |> select(season_code, start_year, url) |> print(n = Inf)
cat("Seasons found:", nrow(seasons), "\n")
```

## Download and import

Each CSV is downloaded to `data/raw` only if it is not already present. In case of a failed download or malformed file, the report stops with the season code instead of silently excluding matches. No `for` loops are needed.

```{r load_data}
dir.create("data/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

required_columns <- c("Date", "HomeTeam", "AwayTeam", "FTHG", "FTAG")

read_season <- function(file_url, season_code) {
  local_file <- file.path("data/raw", paste0("I1_", season_code, ".csv"))

  if (!file.exists(local_file) || file.info(local_file)$size == 0) {
    message("Downloading season ", season_code)
    tryCatch(
      download.file(file_url, destfile = local_file,
                    mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE),
      error = function(e) {
        if (file.exists(local_file)) unlink(local_file)
        stop("Download failed for season ", season_code,
             ": ", conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE)
      }
    )
    Sys.sleep(0.5)
  }

  if (!file.exists(local_file) || file.info(local_file)$size == 0) {
    stop("Missing or empty CSV for season ", season_code, call. = FALSE)
  }

  data <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(read_csv(
      local_file,
      col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
      show_col_types = FALSE,
      progress = FALSE
    )),
    error = function(e) stop("Cannot read season ", season_code,
                              ": ", conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE)
  )

  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_columns, names(data))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("Missing columns in season ", season_code, ": ",
         paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  issues <- problems(data)
  if (nrow(issues) > 0) {
    message("Season ", season_code, ": ", nrow(issues),
            " CSV parsing issue(s). Inspect problems(read_csv(file)).")
  }

  data |> select(all_of(required_columns))
}

serie_a_master <- map2_dfr(
  seasons$url,
  seasons$season_code,
  read_season
)

cat("Rows before filtering:", nrow(serie_a_master), "\n")
```

## Keep valid dates and required columns

The assignment asks to discard missing dates. Empty or whitespace-only dates are also treated as missing. The two goal columns are converted to numeric for subsequent analysis; the original date strings are preserved because CSVs may have different date formats.

```{r clean_data}
valid_dates <- serie_a_master |>
  filter(!is.na(Date), str_trim(Date) != "") |>
  select(all_of(required_columns)) |>
  mutate(
    FTHG = readr::parse_number(FTHG),
    FTAG = readr::parse_number(FTAG)
  )

stopifnot(identical(names(valid_dates), required_columns))

cat("Rows before filtering:", nrow(serie_a_master), "\n")
cat("Rows after filtering:", nrow(valid_dates), "\n")
```

## Data Quality Checks

```{r data-quality}
quality_summary <- valid_dates |>
  summarise(
    matches = n(),
    missing_dates = sum(is.na(Date) | str_trim(Date) == ""),
    missing_home_teams = sum(is.na(HomeTeam) | str_trim(HomeTeam) == ""),
    missing_away_teams = sum(is.na(AwayTeam) | str_trim(AwayTeam) == ""),
    missing_home_goals = sum(is.na(FTHG)),
    missing_away_goals = sum(is.na(FTAG))
  )

quality_summary
```

The combined Serie A dataset contains **`r format(nrow(serie_a_master), big.mark = ",")`** observations. After removing observations with missing or blank dates, **`r format(nrow(valid_dates), big.mark = ",")`** records remain. These totals are computed from the imported data, rather than entered manually.

Matches without a final score are excluded **only for the subsequent team statistics**, not from the requested Challenge 2 dataset.

```{r completed-matches}
completed_matches <- valid_dates |>
  filter(!is.na(HomeTeam), str_trim(HomeTeam) != "",
         !is.na(AwayTeam), str_trim(AwayTeam) != "",
         !is.na(FTHG), !is.na(FTAG))

cat("Matches with complete results:", nrow(completed_matches), "\n")
```

# Challenge 3: Team Statistics


```{r}


library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# 1. Identify the outcome of each match
matches_outcome <- completed_matches |>
  mutate(
    outcome = case_when(
      FTHG > FTAG ~ "H",
      FTHG < FTAG ~ "A",
      TRUE ~ "P"
    )
  )

# 2. Statistics for home teams
home_stats <- matches_outcome |>
  transmute(
    team = HomeTeam,
    result = case_when(
      outcome == "H" ~ "wins",
      outcome == "A" ~ "losses",
      TRUE ~ "draws"
    )
  )

# 3. Statistics for away teams
away_stats <- matches_outcome |>
  transmute(
    team = AwayTeam,
    result = case_when(
      outcome == "A" ~ "wins",
      outcome == "H" ~ "losses",
      TRUE ~ "draws"
    )
  )

# 4. Combine home and away results
all_results <- bind_rows(home_stats, away_stats)

# 5. Count results and transform into wide format
team_statistics <- all_results |>
  count(team, result, name = "n") |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = result,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  mutate(
    matches = wins + losses + draws,
    points = wins * 3 + draws,
    points_per_match = points / matches
  ) |>
  select(
    team,
    matches,
    wins,
    losses,
    draws,
    points,
    points_per_match
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(points_per_match))

# Display results
print(team_statistics, n = Inf)
```




# Challenge 4: Data Questions

Three questions to investigate (answers are intentionally not provided):

1. Which team has the highest average points per match since 1993? 
2. Come variano  i campioni e i retrocessi
3. Quali sono le regioni dove abbiamo piu campioni o piu squadre  delle regioni?
